findings.title: Two tracked files carry unrotated Power Automate SAS signatures and are absent from the secret baseline, so the repository's own secret gate exits non-zero
findings.basis: `node tests/check-secrets.mjs` exits 1; 2 carrier(s) are not listed in tests/secrets-baseline.txt.

findings.title: A 16 MB build artefact holding the majority of the repository's distinct SAS signatures is tracked, and tracked tooling reads it at runtime
findings.basis: ECM_DOCS_DEV.zip is 16,783,981 of 19,080,145 tracked bytes (88.0%), carries 31 distinct signatures across 18 members, and 2 tracked file(s) depend on it programmatically.

findings.title: The design system exists as two live forks that have drifted apart in both directions
findings.basis: 18 counterpart relation(s) span document-portal/ds/ and styles/dgo-design-system/: 2 byte-identical, 2 where one side is a clean superset, 8 with content unique to BOTH sides, and 6 with no counterpart at all. Only the identical pairs can be resolved by deleting one side.

findings.title: Shipped source comments cite verification tooling that does not exist in the repository
findings.basis: 7 stale reference(s) in 5 code file(s) name a test, tool or evidence file that resolves nowhere in scope.

findings.title: A directory that declares itself superseded is kept alive only by citations from the directory whose own future is unresolved, and one of its files is a signature carrier
findings.basis: docs/forensic/177d992/README.md declares the directory superseded and states its own retention rationale; the directory holds 4 file(s) totalling 40,279 bytes, one of which is an unbaselined signature carrier, and every incoming citation originates inside the unresolved set of H-07.

findings.title: Documentation describes a pre-consolidation directory layout that no longer exists
findings.basis: 32 stale reference(s) in 8 documentation file(s) point at trees that are absent from the working tree, from git-ignore rules and from the tracked archive.

findings.title: A second forensic evidence directory and one portal README have no incoming tracked reference and no signal that resolves whether they are current
findings.basis: 10 file(s) totalling 118,110 bytes are unreachable from every Phase 1 root and carry no duplicate or supersession signal in Phase 2.

findings.title: Two design-system token sheets are byte-identical across both trees, so one is pure redundancy that can drift at any time
findings.basis: 4 file(s) in 2 sha256 group(s) are byte-identical, wasting 7,071 bytes; both copies are asset-referenced, so neither is dead.

recommendations.action: Rotate every Power Automate signature reachable from the tree, then reconcile tests/secrets-baseline.txt with the carriers that remain
recommendations.prerequisite: Rotation happens in Power Automate first. Editing the tree revokes nothing.
recommendations.risk_if_done: None to runtime: no tracked runtime module imports the affected files.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: The secret gate stays red, so it can no longer distinguish a genuinely new leak from the known ones - the ratchet is inert while it is failing.
recommendations.note: Do this before any removal recommendation below: several of them delete a carrier, and a deleted carrier is still readable in Git history.

recommendations.action: Decouple tracked tooling from ECM_DOCS_DEV.zip, then untrack the archive and publish it out-of-band
recommendations.prerequisite: R-01 must land first (the archive holds 31 distinct signatures), and scripts/setup-local.mjs, tests/secrets-baseline.txt must stop depending on the archive.
recommendations.risk_if_done: `npm run setup` stops working until it sources endpoints from somewhere else; tests/check-secrets.mjs fails on a stale baseline row unless the baseline is edited in the same change.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: 88.0% of the repository stays as a tracked credential-bearing artefact that GitHub serves over HTTPS to anyone with read access.
recommendations.note: The repository already states this intent in tests/secrets-baseline.txt; Phase 3 only supplies the blocker list needed to act on it.

recommendations.action: Pick one design-system tree as the source of truth and make the other consume it, reconciling the two-way drift first
recommendations.prerequisite: A per-counterpart diff review, because outside the identical pairs no copy is a superset.
recommendations.risk_if_done: Visual regression across both portals; the two barrels load different files in different orders, so a naive merge changes the cascade.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: Every fix must be applied twice, and a fix applied once silently makes the portals disagree.
recommendations.blast_radius: 18 counterpart relation(s) across two runtime surfaces (styles/index.css and document-portal/ds/ds.css).
recommendations.note: 8 relation(s) have unique content on both sides and 6 file(s) exist on one side only. Deleting either tree loses content.

recommendations.action: Either add the cited verification tooling or delete the claim from the comment
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: Shipped source asserts a guarantee the repository cannot honour, which is the failure mode the CI module-graph job exists to prevent.
recommendations.note: The lowest-cost item on this list: no runtime behaviour depends on any of these lines.

recommendations.action: Rotate the carrier inside docs/forensic/177d992/, then settle the directory together with R-07 rather than on its own
recommendations.prerequisite: R-01, because one of these files is an unbaselined signature carrier; and R-07, because every citation of this directory originates inside the set R-07 leaves undecided.
recommendations.risk_if_done: 2 tracked file(s) cite this directory, and 2 of them sit inside the set R-07 leaves undecided; removing either side alone breaks the citations or strands the other.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: 40,279 bytes stay in a state no single decision can resolve, and the directory keeps a live credential in the tree.
recommendations.note: This is deliberately not a removal recommendation. The directory's README already states why it is retained and qualifies rather than forbids citation, so the evidence does not support deleting it; what the evidence does support is rotating its credential and resolving it jointly with R-07.

recommendations.action: Correct the documented directory layout, or mark the affected documents as historical records of a layout that has since changed
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: Onboarding and audit readers are pointed at paths that do not exist, which is how the pre-consolidation layout keeps propagating into new documents.
recommendations.note: Several of these documents are audit records; correcting them in place may be wrong. Dating them is a legitimate alternative and is why this is not a delete recommendation.

recommendations.action: Ask the owner whether the second forensic directory and document-portal/README.md are still wanted; record the answer either way
recommendations.prerequisite: An owner decision. Phase 2 explicitly declined to convert unreferenced into unnecessary.
recommendations.risk_if_done: Deleting a current-but-unlinked audit record would destroy evidence.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: 118,110 bytes stay in an unresolved state and will be re-surfaced by every future audit at the same cost.
recommendations.note: Being unreferenced is not being unnecessary. This item asks a question; it does not recommend removal.

recommendations.action: Fold the two byte-identical token sheets into the single source of truth chosen in R-03
recommendations.prerequisite: R-03 must choose the surviving tree first.
recommendations.risk_if_done: A cascade change if the surviving copy is imported at a different point in the barrel order.
recommendations.risk_if_deferred: 7,071 bytes of exact redundancy remain, and two files that agree today can disagree after any single-sided edit.
recommendations.note: Strictly a subset of R-03; listed separately because it is the part that carries no drift risk and can be done mechanically once the source of truth is chosen.
